intent: Correct merged PR #1112 by moving Episode Ledger sequence allocation into an interprocess-locked writer, rehydrating event IDs, logical delivery keys, and per-episode high-water marks in one pass, and extending the canonical RuntimeStateStore with a transactional durable episode-event outbox so session-event persistence and observation enqueue are atomic and append-before-ack replay is exactly once across failures and restarts while preserving torn-tail recovery.

negative_controls.name: duplicate-episode-sequence-write-must-not-succeed
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; import tempfile; from dharma_swarm.episode_ledger import EpisodeEvent, EpisodeLedgerWriter; d=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(); w=EpisodeLedgerWriter(Path(d.name) / 'episode.jsonl'); a=EpisodeEvent.new(event_type='attempt_started', episode_id='ep_negative', attempt_id='at_a', sequence=1); b=EpisodeEvent.new(event_type='attempt_started', episode_id='ep_negative', attempt_id='at_b', sequence=1); assert w.append(a); assert w.append(b)"

interface_mismatches: PR #1112 SessionLedger instances cache independent next-sequence values for one stable episode, so concurrent writers can persist distinct events at the same sequence.
PR #1112 commits a runtime-state session event before its Episode Ledger observation append without a durable retry record, so append failure or process exit can permanently lose the observation.
PR #1112 rehydrates EpisodeLedgerWriter and then separately rescans the complete JSONL history for the next sequence, doubling unbounded startup work.
honest_blockers: The outbox and file lock provide single-host process durability; they do not claim distributed multi-host ordering over a shared network filesystem.
Exact-head hosted CI and independent review remain required before integration.
Human merge authority remains required; this branch must not self-merge.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the additive outbox schema and methods, locked writer allocation, SessionLedger drain path, focused tests, and this packet together. Existing session_events and Episode Ledger JSONL rows remain readable; no destructive migration or runtime-data rewrite is part of the packet.
